items.title: What Is It?
transcript: Anna: Pete, hi! Hi, we are here!
Pete: Hi, Anna! Hi, Marsha!
Pete: How are you two?
Marsha: I am great!
Anna: You know, Pete, I am new to D.C. The city is big.
Pete: Yeah. But you learn a little more every day. How's the new apartment?
Anna: The new apartment is great! Let's get coffee!
Marsha: Anna, do you have a pen?
Anna: Yes. I have a pen in my bag. I have a ...
Pete: It is not a pen. It is a book. It is a big book.
Marsha: It is not a pen, Anna ... a toy?
Pete: And it is a pillow!
Marsha: Anna, it is a map.
Pete: Why do you have a map of the world?
Anna: Pete, Marsha. Now I know I have a pen.
Pete: And now you have a lamp.
Anna: I have a pen! Let's get coffee!

questions.stem: What does Pete first say Anna has found instead of a pen?
questions.explanation: Pete first identifies the object as a big book.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: follow the sequence of objects Anna takes from her bag.

questions.stem: What does Marsha think one object might be?
questions.explanation: Marsha suggests that one object may be a toy.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: compare Marsha's guess with the other object guesses.

questions.stem: What does Pete identify after the toy guess?
questions.explanation: Pete calls the next object a pillow.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: keep the object sequence in order.

questions.stem: What is Anna's map of?
questions.explanation: Pete asks why Anna has a map of the world.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify the map's stated scope.

questions.stem: What do Anna and her friends decide to do?
questions.explanation: Anna returns to the plan to get coffee at the end.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify the plan repeated at the ending.

items.title: Where Are You?
transcript: Anna: Hello, everyone! Today my friend Marsha is at her friend's house. She says it is beautiful. I want to see this house! Here we are!
Anna: Marsha, I am in the kitchen! It is a beautiful kitchen!
Marsha: It is beautiful. We cook in the kitchen.
Anna: I eat in the kitchen.
Marsha: We relax in the living room.
Anna: I relax in the living room. Marsha, let's go upstairs!
Marsha: Anna? Where are you?
Anna: Marsha, I am in the bathroom! I wash in the bathroom.
Marsha: I am in the bedroom. We sleep in the bedroom.
Anna: I sleep in the bedroom!

questions.stem: Where is Anna when she first arrives?
questions.explanation: Anna says she is in the kitchen at the start of the visit.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify the opening location from the dialogue.

questions.stem: What do Marsha and Anna say people do in the kitchen?
questions.explanation: Marsha says they cook there; Anna says she eats there.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: compare both speakers' statements about the kitchen.

questions.stem: Where do they relax?
questions.explanation: Marsha names the living room as the place where they relax.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: locate the statement about relaxing.

questions.stem: Where does Anna say she washes?
questions.explanation: Anna directly connects washing with the bathroom.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify Anna's upstairs location and activity.

questions.stem: Where do Marsha and Anna say they sleep?
questions.explanation: Both speakers connect sleeping with the bedroom.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify the final room and its activity.

items.title: Where Is the Gym?
transcript: Anna: Hi there! I'm Anna and I live in Washington, D.C. Every day I learn more about this great city. People in Washington like to work out! Oh, hi, Pete. How's it going?
Pete: Hi, Anna. It's going great. How's it going with you?
Anna: Things are awesome! Pete, I want to work out. Where is the gym?
Pete: The gym is across from the lounge. It's next to the mailroom. Go that way.
Anna: Thanks, Pete!
Pete: No, Anna! Not that way! Go that way!
Anna: Oh, Pete. This is not the gym.
Pete: That's right, Anna. This is the mailroom.
Pete: The gym is across from the lounge.
Pete: The gym is across from the lounge. It is behind the lobby.
Anna: This is not a gym. This is a parking garage.
Anna: This is not a gym. This is a rooftop.
Pete: I want to work out too! Join me!
Anna: I'm good.

questions.stem: Why does Anna ask Pete about the gym?
options: She wants to mail a letter
questions.explanation: Anna says she wants to work out before asking for directions.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: connect Anna's stated goal with her question.

questions.stem: What place is next to the gym?
questions.explanation: Pete says the gym is next to the mailroom.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: follow Pete's directions and Anna's first mistaken stop.

questions.stem: Which place does Anna visit but discover is not the gym?
questions.explanation: Anna identifies one mistaken stop as a parking garage.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify one of Anna's mistaken destinations.

questions.stem: Where is the gym in relation to the lobby?
questions.explanation: Pete says the gym is behind the lobby.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: compare the repeated directions.

questions.stem: What does Pete invite Anna to do at the end?
questions.explanation: Pete says he wants to work out too and invites Anna to join him.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: understand the final invitation.

items.title: What Are You Doing?
transcript: Caty: Come in. Well, Anna, welcome. I am your boss, Caty Weaver. But, please call me Caty.
Anna: Thank you, Ms. Weaver.
Caty: Just Caty.
Caty: Are you excited?
Anna: Yes, I am excited!
Caty: I am busy. Please meet your co-workers. But remember, they are busy working.
Anna: Hi there! I'm Anna.
Anne: Hi, Anna. I'm Anne.
Anna: Nice to meet you. What are you doing?
Anne: Um, I'm writing.
Anna: I am sorry!
Jonathan: And people all around the world are waiting to hear news about the next president.
Anna: Jonathan, hi! Remember me? I live in your building.
Anna: What are you doing?
Jonathan: I am doing my show!
Anna: Oh, sorry. Are you recording?
Jonathan: Yes! And now I have to record again!
Amelia: The word of the day is social. Social is an adjective.
Anna: Nice to meet you! What are you doing?
Amelia: I'm reading.
Anna: Are you reading the news?
Amelia: No, I'm reading for my show.
Anna: This day is not going well.
Caty: Anna! What are you doing?
Anna: I am bothering people, Ms. Weaver.
Caty: Let's go to my office and talk.

questions.stem: What is Anne doing when Anna first meets her?
questions.explanation: Anne says she is writing.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: distinguish the co-workers' activities.

questions.stem: What is Jonathan doing in the studio?
questions.explanation: Jonathan says he is doing his show and recording again after the interruption.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: use the studio context and Jonathan's response.

questions.stem: What is Amelia reading for?
questions.explanation: Amelia explains that she is reading for her show.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: distinguish Amelia's reading from Anna's guess.

questions.stem: Where does Caty ask Anna to go so they can talk?
questions.explanation: Caty asks Anna to go to her office.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: follow the final instruction.

questions.stem: How does Anna feel the day is going?
questions.explanation: Anna says the day is not going well after interrupting her co-workers.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: infer Anna's view from her comment and events.

items.title: Are You Busy?
transcript: Anna: Hello, everyone. Here I am at my new job! Today I want to apologize to my co-workers.
Anna: Hi, Anne. Are you busy?
Anne: Yes. At 10 a.m. I am writing. Every day I do my morning show.
Anna: Hi, Jonathan. Are you busy?
Jonathan: When the studio light is on, I am recording my evening show.
Anna: Sorry about yesterday.
Jonathan: No worries.
Anna: May I see the studio?
Jonathan: Maybe another time. Right now I am busy.
Anna: Hi, Amelia! Are you busy?
Amelia: I'm a little busy.
Anna: I want to say I'm sorry for yesterday.
Amelia: It's okay. Come by this afternoon.
Caty: Are you busy?
Anna: Yes, Ms. Weaver. I am busy.
Caty: My office. 5:00 p.m.
Caty: Come in.
Co-workers: Surprise!
Anna: A party! Awesome! And I still have my job!

questions.stem: What is Anne doing at 10 a.m.?
questions.explanation: Anne states her activity at 10 a.m.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: connect the time with Anne's activity.

questions.stem: What does Jonathan do when the studio light is on?
questions.explanation: Jonathan explains what the studio light means for his work.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: understand Jonathan's work routine.

questions.stem: When does Amelia invite Anna to come by?
questions.explanation: Amelia tells Anna to come by this afternoon.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: distinguish Amelia's invitation from Caty's appointment.

questions.stem: What time does Caty tell Anna to come to her office?
questions.explanation: Caty gives Anna the appointment time.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: compare the appointment with other times mentioned.

questions.stem: What surprise do Anna's co-workers have for her?
questions.explanation: The co-workers surprise Anna with a party, and she learns she still has her job.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: understand the ending and the reason Anna feels relieved.

items.title: Is It Cold?
transcript: Anna: In Washington, DC, the weather changes often. One day is cold and windy. But the next day is warm and sunny. So every day I check the forecast.
Phone: Today it is 18 degrees ... eighteen degrees Celsius.
Anna: Eighteen degrees! That is cold! Oh, Celsius. That is 65 degrees Fahrenheit. That's warm.
Phone: Yes, Anna. It is warm.
Anna: Is it windy today?
Phone: No, it is not windy today.
Anna: Is it sunny today?
Phone: Yes, Anna. It is sunny.
Anna: Is it snowy today?
Phone: No, Anna. It is not snowy.
Anna: Today the weather is warm and sunny -- great for seeing Washington, DC.
Anna: Phone! It is not warm and sunny! It is cold and windy and snowy!
Phone: Anna, it is not cold, windy, or snowy. It is warm and sunny ... in Mexico City, Mexico.
Anna: Washington weather changes often. Remember to check the forecast -- the right forecast.

questions.stem: What number does the phone give for the temperature?
questions.explanation: The phone first reports 18 degrees, then clarifies the Celsius scale.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: hear the number and its unit clarification.

questions.stem: What does Anna first think about 18 degrees?
questions.explanation: Anna initially reacts to the number before learning it is Celsius.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: follow Anna's reaction before and after the unit is named.

questions.stem: What is 18 degrees Celsius in Fahrenheit in this conversation?
questions.explanation: Anna converts the temperature to 65 degrees Fahrenheit.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: connect the Celsius and Fahrenheit numbers.

questions.stem: Which city's forecast was the phone giving at the end?
questions.explanation: The phone reveals that the warm, sunny forecast is for Mexico City.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: understand the final correction to the forecast location.

questions.stem: What should Anna remember to check?
questions.explanation: Anna concludes that she needs the forecast for the correct city.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify the lesson Anna states at the ending.

items.title: Come Over to My Place
transcript: Anna: Today my friend Ashley is coming over. I am showing her my new apartment.
Ashley: I'm coming to your apartment. Where is your apartment?
Anna: My apartment is near the Columbia Heights Metro.
Anna: Exit the Metro and turn right. Then at the bus station turn left. Then walk straight ahead.
Ashley: Exit Metro, turn right, turn left, then go straight ahead?
Anna: Yes. My apartment is near a coffee shop.
Ashley: Which coffee shop? There are three coffee shops.
Anna: My apartment is across from a big department store.
Ashley: A big department store? Ah, I see it!
Anna: I love having my friends over. Come on!

questions.stem: Who is coming to Anna's apartment?
questions.explanation: Anna says Ashley is coming over.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify the visitor and follow her arrival.

questions.stem: What is Anna's apartment near?
questions.explanation: Anna uses the Metro station as the first location clue.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify the starting landmark in Anna's directions.

questions.stem: After leaving the Metro, which way should Ashley turn first?
questions.explanation: Anna's first direction is to turn right after exiting the Metro.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: follow the direction sequence in order.

questions.stem: What landmark is across from Anna's apartment?
questions.explanation: Anna gives the department store as the clearer landmark.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: distinguish the final landmark from the earlier coffee-shop clue.

questions.stem: Why does Ashley ask Anna to name a coffee shop?
options: She cannot find the bus station
questions.explanation: Ashley says there are three coffee shops, so that clue is not specific enough.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: understand why Ashley asks for a more specific landmark.

items.title: This Is My Neighborhood
transcript: Anna: Before we get ice cream, I need to return three books to the library. Where is the library?
Marsha: It is on this street on the corner.
Anna: These are letters to my family and friends back home ... four letters! Is there a post office near here?
Marsha: The post office is far from here. But there is a mailbox across from the store.
Anna: Now I need to buy stamps.
Marsha: Do you have cash?
Anna: No. Is there a bank near here?
Marsha: There is a bank behind you.
Anna: Now I have cash. I can buy stamps.
Marsha: That store sells stamps.
Anna: I have stamps.
Anna and Marsha: Ice cream!
Anna: I love my new neighborhood! Everything is near our apartment!

questions.stem: What does Anna need to return to the library?
questions.explanation: Anna says she needs to return three books before getting ice cream.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: follow Anna's errands and identify the first one.

questions.stem: What does Anna discover inside the books?
questions.explanation: Anna realizes the books contain letters for her family and friends.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: connect the letters to Anna's next errand.

questions.stem: Where is the mailbox?
questions.explanation: Marsha gives the mailbox location when the post office is too far away.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: distinguish the mailbox clue from the library and bank locations.

questions.stem: Where is the bank in relation to Anna?
questions.explanation: Anna says the bank is behind Marsha, who is speaking to her; the location is given as behind you.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: interpret the direction given during the stamp errand.

questions.stem: What do Anna and Marsha plan to get after the errands?
questions.explanation: They say 'Ice cream!' after Anna gets the stamps.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: understand the errands' final goal.

items.title: Meet My Family
transcript: Anna: I'm thinking about my family. I'm feeling homesick. I have some photos.
Anna: This is my mother and this is my father. They are rodeo clowns. They make jokes at a rodeo. They make people laugh.
Anna: That is my Aunt Lavender. She is my mom's sister. She loves gardening and makes spoons.
Anna: This is my Uncle John. He is my father's brother. He's a chicken farmer and makes guitars.
Anna: They are my cousins. They are my Uncle John's daughter and son. They raise sheep and make sweaters.
Anna: I do feel better. Thanks for listening. Washington, DC is my new home. But I like remembering my old home, too.

questions.stem: Why does Anna show Marsha her family photos?
questions.explanation: Anna says she is thinking about her family and feeling homesick.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: connect Anna's feelings to her decision to share photos.

questions.stem: What do Anna's parents do?
questions.explanation: Anna describes both parents as rodeo clowns.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify the parents' work.

questions.stem: What does Aunt Lavender enjoy?
questions.explanation: Anna says her aunt loves gardening and makes spoons.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: distinguish the aunt's interests from other family members' jobs.

questions.stem: Which two things does Uncle John do?
questions.explanation: Anna describes Uncle John as a chicken farmer who also makes guitars.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: combine both details about Uncle John's work.

questions.stem: What do Anna's cousins do?
options: They raise sheep and make sweaters
questions.correctAnswer: They raise sheep and make sweaters
questions.explanation: Anna says her cousins raise sheep and make sweaters.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify the cousins' shared activities.

items.title: Happy Birthday, William Shakespeare!
transcript: Anna: I feel bored. When I feel bored I always look for something unusual to do. I hear music. Let's go see!
Rebecca: It's a big birthday party for the writer William Shakespeare.
Anna: This is a drum band. I never listen to a drum band. But today I am listening to a drum band because it's Shakespeare's birthday!
Anna: This is a puppet show. I never watch puppet shows. But today I am watching a puppet show because it's Shakespeare's birthday!
Anna: Seeing the Queen of England is very unusual! Your majesty!
Anna: This is sword fighting. I never sword fight. But today I am sword fighting because it's Shakespeare's birthday!
Anna: Today, I am not bored because it is William Shakespeare's birthday!

questions.stem: Whose birthday is the party celebrating?
questions.explanation: Rebecca explains that the party is for William Shakespeare.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify the event that brings the activities together.

questions.stem: What music performance does Anna hear?
questions.explanation: Anna hears and watches a drum band at the celebration.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify one event Anna experiences.

questions.stem: What kind of show does Anna watch?
questions.explanation: Anna describes watching a puppet show.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: identify the show among the unusual activities.

questions.stem: Whom does Anna call very unusual to see in Washington, D.C.?
questions.explanation: Anna contrasts seeing the Queen with more usual sights in Washington, D.C.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: understand Anna's usual-versus-unusual comparison.

questions.stem: Why does Anna say she is no longer bored?
options: She is enjoying unusual birthday activities
She has found a new job
questions.correctAnswer: She is enjoying unusual birthday activities
questions.explanation: The celebration gives Anna several unusual things to see and do.

mainSegment.basis: Whole conversation: infer the reason from the events and Anna's final statement.
